entities.summary:
Mugain, daughter of Eochaid Feidlech, is a legendary queen in the Ulster Cycle of Irish mythology; characterized as the 'Strumpet wife of Conchobar mac Nessa', the king of Ulster. She had a son with him named Glaisne and was also a sister of Medb by paternity. Mugain's life is shrouded in myth and legend, with few concrete details available. She is often depicted as a symbol of feminine power and agency in ancient Irish society.

In the Ulster Cycle, Mugain plays a significant role in the story of Conchobar mac Nessa's reign, serving as a symbol of his power and authority. Her relationship with Conchobar is complex and multifaceted, with some accounts portraying her as a willing participant in his intrigues and others depicting her as a victim of his machinations.

Despite the limited historical record, Mugain's legacy continues to be felt in Irish mythology and folklore. Her story has been retold and reinterpreted over the centuries, with many modern adaptations and reinterpretations of her character appearing in literature, film, and art.

One of the most striking aspects of Mugain's story is her association with the concept of 'strumpet,' a term used to describe a woman who is seen as promiscuous or unfaithful. This label has been used to describe Mugain's relationship with Conchobar, highlighting the societal pressures and expectations placed on women in ancient Irish society.

In conclusion, Mugain's life and legacy are a testament to the enduring power of myth and legend in shaping our understanding of the past. Her story continues to captivate and inspire audiences, offering a unique window into the culture and society of ancient Ireland.
